subject: Environment activation & handoff — onboarding matrix and network items
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Rivera <c.rivera@novamed.com>, Nora Patel <nora.patel@novamed.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Environment activation & handoff — onboarding matrix and network items

Hi Carlos / Nora —

Following up from yesterday’s call with a compact onboarding matrix (attached) so we can lock the POC activation window. This MAP is focused specifically on the environment activation tasks we discussed: org setup, API key provisioning, IP allowlist, and VPC peering. Key asks below so we can target the week of May 9 for an initial smoke test.

Top-line requests for your networking team:
- VPC peering details: preferred peering model (AWS VPC peering vs Transit Gateway), peer VPC ASN (if using TGW), and the target CIDR(s) you want Redwood to peer with.
- IP allowlist: provide a short list of public egress IPs or ranges we should add to your firewall for the sandbox; if you prefer, we can provide a temporary testing range.
- API access: confirm whether you want API keys per-team or a shared service account. If service account, please provide the identity name and preferred key rotation cadence.
- Compliance note: we’ve included a short retention/telemetry blurb in the MAP; let us know if your security team needs a separate evidence bundle (SOC/comms).

Attachments: Redwood_NovaMed_MAP_v1.2.pdf (MAP + environment matrix) and firewall-template.csv (format we use for IP allowlist).

Proposed timeline (high level):
- By Wed May 5: NovaMed provides ASN/CIDR and allowlist ranges
- Thu May 6: Redwood provisions sandbox org + initial API key(s) and shares credentials via Vault link
- Week of May 9: network peering & smoke tests; first traffic validation

If this looks good I’ll assign owners and lock calendar invites. Thanks — short reply with who on your side owns the peering item and API/key decisions is all I need to proceed.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0197

From: Carlos Rivera <c.rivera@novamed.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nora Patel <nora.patel@novamed.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Environment activation & handoff — onboarding matrix and network items

Thanks Hannah —

Appreciate the clear matrix. Quick answers from our side:
- Peering model: we prefer AWS VPC peering for the POC (no TGW for this phase).
- CIDRs: primary workload VPC is 10.40.0.0/16 (we will confirm if we can spare a /20 for testing).
- ASN: 64520 (we're on standard private ASN for peering).
- IP allowlist: attaching our current firewall inventory; for now please use the temporary egress range 34.201.64.0/20 for test traffic.
- API keys: prefer a shared service account for the POC; request that keys be rotated weekly during the evaluation.

I’ve attached a CSV export of our firewall rules. Our network lead (Nora) will follow up with the peering ticket and schedule a 30-min handoff with your infra folks tomorrow or Tue.

-Carlos
Carlos Rivera
Cloud Ops Manager | NovaMed
c.rivera@novamed.com

Thanks Carlos — good progress. Internal owners and a concise checklist so we don’t lose momentum:

Redwood owners
- Sandbox org & API keys (provision + Vault link): Jordan Blake (owner) — target Thu May 6
- Peering playbook & routing test plan: Karthik Iyer (owner) — coordinate with NovaMed network on scheduling
- Security/retention evidence & telemetry: Evelyn Hart (owner) — will prepare the short bundle (logs, retention policy, minimal audit)

Open items for NovaMed
- Confirm whether you can carve out a /20 (preferred) or we proceed with 10.40.0.0/16 for initial peering
- Finalize the list of public egress IPs to allow (Carlos mentioned 34.201.64.0/20 for test)
- Confirm the service account name and the contact for automated key rotations (weekly during POC)

I’ll create the calendar invites for the peering handoff and the smoke-test slot. For the smoke test we’ll run: simple tokenized inference, TTL < 250ms single-token, and a short embedding batch to validate throughput.

-Jordan

Hi Hannah / team —

We’re ready to proceed with the timeline as proposed. Confirming the details for provisioning and peering:
- Peering model: AWS VPC peering confirmed.
- Peer CIDR for testing: 10.40.128.0/20 (confirmed available).
- ASN: 64520 (as noted).
- Public egress ranges to allow: 34.201.64.0/20 and 3.237.120.0/21 (these are our NAT egress IP pools).
- Service account: nova-poc-redwood@novamed-svc (please provision keys scoped to "eval:sandbox" role).

I’ve opened the internal ticket to accept the peering request once we receive your console-side configuration; ETA for the ticket is Tue May 10. In the meantime I attached the signed network confidentiality addendum and our firewall export.

Next steps from Redwood: please provision the sandbox org and post the Vault link for credentials. We’ll accept peering once the AWS request comes through and then schedule the smoke test for May 11 (10:00am PT).

Thanks — looking forward to the smoke test.

Nora Patel
Director, Cloud Infrastructure | NovaMed
